q: pour-over coffee with a basic kettle
how to brew pour over coffee
pour over coffee without gooseneck kettle
best way to brew pour over coffee
a: To brew pour-over coffee with a basic kettle (no gooseneck): 1. Heat water to 195-205F (just off boiling). 2. Place a paper filter in your pour-over cone (Hario V60, Chemex, or Kalita Wave) and rinse it with hot water to remove paper taste and preheat the brewer. Discard rinse water. 3. Add medium-fine ground coffee (about 15g per 250ml of water). 4. Pour a small amount of water (about double the coffee weight) over the grounds to bloom - let it sit for 30 seconds to release CO2. 5. Pour the remaining water slowly in circular motions starting from the center and working outward. Without a gooseneck kettle, pour slowly and steadily from a height of about 2-3 inches. If pouring too fast causes splashing, use a spoon to control the flow or pour in stages. 6. Total brew time should be 2.5-3.5 minutes. 7. Remove the filter and enjoy. Pro tips: a chopstick or spoon can help control flow from a regular kettle. Pre-wetting the filter and blooming are essential steps regardless of kettle type. The most important variables are grind size, water temperature, and pouring speed.
